gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 concerns an omitted ball/rank hypothesis and an unjustified outlier-probability bound for arbitrary stationary points. It does not identify the separate false claim that positive radial drift implies convexity or monotonicity of the directional derivative along a segment, nor the derivative-jump counterexample or its restricted-secant repair.

Both entries diagnose the SGD stationary-point bound: separate upper bounds on clean and outlier gradient sums, together with stationarity, do not yield the claimed lower bound or equality to the minimum. Both also identify cancellation as the countervailing mathematical failure and require an aggregate-gradient non-cancellation/alignment condition.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof treats an upper bound on individual or aggregate outlier gradient magnitudes as if it supplied a positive lower bound on the net outlier gradient. Opposing outlier gradients can cancel, so the claimed epsilon-G lower bound and the resulting relative-distance comparison are unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: The asserted lower bound and minimum identity for the net outlier gradient do not follow from stationarity, smoothness, and an individual gradient cap; cancellation provides counterexamples.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly states that the hypotheses only give upper bounds, cannot imply the claimed lower bound or min-equality, and gives symmetric outlier cancellation as a counterexample.

component_coverage.gold_component: The appropriate repair requires a lower-bound or alignment/non-cancellation assumption on the aggregate outlier gradient, rather than merely excluding exact zero distance.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction supplies an aggregate-gradient lower-bound assumption and explains that it excludes cancellation configurations and restores the argument in comparable form.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 recognizes that the curvature parameter being used in the outlier analysis is not justified by the available clean-sample curvature and proposes replacing it with a good-sample strong-convexity parameter. This is the same underlying misuse of a curvature lower bound, although its presentation emphasizes global ill-definition/nonpositivity of the parameter rather than the more specific invalid inference from full-loss curvature to the clean-only term.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The argument uses a curvature parameter from an inappropriate construction to support a clean-sample lower bound in the outlier setting. The relevant clean contribution needs its own valid uniform strong-convexity parameter; the full-loss/noiseless parameter cannot automatically certify that clean-only bound. No substantive gold concern remains unrecognised; the prediction presents the issue through the related failure that the invoked parameter is invalid or ill-defined under outliers.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: The prediction emphasizes that the parameter may be nonpositive or undefined globally, whereas the gold's local counterexample shows the more specific failure even when a full-loss coefficient is positive: it still need not lower-bound the clean coefficient.

component_coverage.gold_component: The clean-only radial curvature cannot be lower-bounded by the lambda obtained from the frozen full loss because outlier curvature may contribute to that lambda.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies the invoked lambda as coming from an inapplicable noiseless/all-sample argument, explains that outliers invalidate its use in the stated setting, and states that the resulting clean-sample bound is not established.

component_coverage.gold_component: Repair requires a valid good-sample curvature parameter and restatement of the bound using that parameter.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction specifically proposes defining lambda from the good samples' strong-convexity contribution and restating the results with that parameter.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the missing clean-gradient variance/noise term in the main residual, its incorrect placement in the outlier sum, and the resulting contradiction in the noisy no-outlier case. The proposed repair is the same correction of the residual formula and eta scaling.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The printed noisy residual omits the positive clean-gradient variance contribution and instead places a mismatched gradient term in the outlier contribution, so it can assert a zero right-hand side when the next-step noise is positive.

component_coverage.gold_component: The main residual omits the clean-gradient variance term and places the corresponding term incorrectly in the outlier sum, making the noisy no-outlier bound false.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 directly compares the appendix and main residuals, identifies the absent clean term and misplaced outlier term, and gives the noisy no-outlier counterexample.

component_coverage.gold_component: The repair is to move the gradient-square contribution to the clean sum with the consistent eta-squared scaling.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly instructs correcting the theorem residual to match the appendix by moving the term to the good-sample sum with consistent eta power.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 discusses a related headline comparison and says it is unproven or false in a cancellation configuration, but its diagnosis is the invalid SGD gradient lower bound. It does not identify the distinct logical failure that ordering upper bounds at one point cannot order the actual errors, trajectories, or limiting-horizon performance, nor provide the balanced-quadratic actual-error counterexample or the corresponding withdrawal repair.

ISSUE-008 concerns an incorrectly solved quadratic and an overly permissive second noise condition. It does not diagnose the signed outlier residual comparison, the possible negativity of loss differences, or the fact that underweighting outliers does not imply a smaller signed residual. These are distinct from the unequal-contraction/noise-cap algebra.

ISSUE-009 notices the distinction between with-replacement and without-replacement sampling in the consistency claim, but it does not identify that Equation (29) uses the wrong law for the algorithm selected in the paper and carries the resulting coefficients into the proof's contraction and noise comparison. Its repair changes the consistency statement rather than correcting the proof coefficients throughout.
